derived_results.claim: The r95 adaptive split rule was reconstructed exactly: accept a shared rectangle at the first N in {128,256,512} whose lower sum exceeds 0.2; otherwise split the longer theta-index dimension at midpoint with ties to mu. This reproduces exactly 46 rectangles and the published five smallest engineering margins.

All interior R~Beta(31/2,3) and U~Beta(37/2,37/2) quantile centers at N=256 and N=512 are enclosed by +/-1.0000001e-8 under independent high-precision CDF checks. Minimum CDF slack: R256 9.3157e-10, R512 4.9845e-10, U256 1.6225e-9, U512 8.9098e-10.

The five smallest-margin rectangles remain positive after probability-box widening, 1e-16 theta widening and independently reconstructed extended-precision arithmetic: 0.20426494580795, 0.37629785823574, 0.48290852102784, 0.69112174992210, 0.70765909709186.

All 46 shared rectangles remain positive under the same extended-precision path. Minimum lower sum is 0.20426494580795 and maximum absolute engineering-vs-extended discrepancy is 8.16e-13; subtracting a diagnostic 1e-9 guard still leaves the global minimum above 0.2042649448.

negative_or_scope_evidence: This is a strong global machine-numerical cross-precision certificate, not yet a fully directed-rounding deterministic theorem; long-double arithmetic and a diagnostic guard do not replace a formal roundoff enclosure.
The N=256/N=512 U-quantile bracket check still uses a high-precision regularized-beta implementation rather than the elementary half-integer recurrence used earlier for a smaller grid.
All results remain restricted to the standardized frozen m=32 NIG/four-corner iid Gaussian setup and the existing analytic negative-ratio premise.
